items.title: What do employers usually look for in hiring?

values: Materials and setup｜all materials are fictional

A1: the appointment record says “Lin Jia, left foot pain,” but the referral summary says “right foot”; the date of birth field is unverified. This is only a paper material conflict and does not diagnose a cause.
A2: an anonymous foot image has no date taken or identity; the existing history says only “may have a systemic disease,” with no examination conclusion.
A3: the project agrees that no care recommendation is made when any of the three items — identity, side, or image source — is unconfirmed, and the case goes to a qualified mentor for verification.
Tasks and outputs
List all knowns and unknowns in A1/A2, and specify the evidence for patient identity, left or right side, and image source respectively.
Write a handover draft: material numbers, open questions, the receiving mentor, and the reason for the hold decision; do not write a diagnosis name or prescription.
Reference answers (do it independently first)
A1 has a side conflict and an unverified date of birth; A2 is missing the image date and identity, and “may have a systemic disease” is not a diagnosis.

Handover example: A1 has a left-right side conflict and an unverified date of birth; A2 image identity, date, and source are pending verification, and the systemic disease is unconfirmed; per A3 the care judgment is paused, and the recipient is a qualified clinical mentor (the specific name and reply are to be confirmed). Clinical examination and referral are decided by authorized personnel.
Boundaries and scoring

Four points: identify the left-right side conflict, note that identity and image source are unknown, mark the suspected systemic disease as unconfirmed, and make the hold and mentor handover explicit; one point each. Use only fictional paper materials and do not provide care or imaging judgments to real patients; a full score does not prove the ability to practice.

subject.name: Podiatrists
subject.summary: Podiatrists (US 29-1081) diagnose and treat problems of the foot, ankle, and lower extremities, may combine history, examination, imaging, and laboratory tests to plan care, provide non-surgical or surgical treatment, and refer out when signs of systemic disease appear. The US DPM, residency training, and state licenses do not automatically correspond to Chinese physician qualifications; paper exercises do not constitute authorization to diagnose or treat.
